body: Oww someone is switching to VS code :D

Did you already thought about how to allow creating your own panels? This could answer this use case in a pretty way. Basically we need to be able to have a connectPanel method that would provide an "isEmpty" or "isRelevant" or "canRefine" boolean to indicate that some widget or custom widget inside has ways to refine.

For a first iteration I would prefer to provide a "disabled" styling to the content of the panel (to indicate it's empty) rather than hiding it completely. What do you think?

We could also think we designers to understand if there's a preferred current way to indicate a widget cannot be used anymore.

I am proposing this because on some widgets it may makes less sense to hide everything:
- slider
- range
- multi ranges

Did you think about other namings for this? Empty is only relevant to list of items I believe, maybe "canRefine"? canRefine true means that the widget can be used to refine, false it means it cannot be used to refine.
I just want to ensure that we tested the "do not hide everything" at least once on our examples and can decide if it's better or not than the hide everything strategy.
I feel it would be easier to understand if we updated the props that will actually means "can no more be used to refine" rather than triggering mount/unmount. What do you think?
Small info: I am waiting for jest to release eslint-plugin-jest to check those mistakes automatically

Proposal:

```txt
The Panel widget wraps other widgets with a consistent panel design. It also reacts, indicates and set CSS classes when widgets are no more relevant for refining (like when a RefinementList becomes empty because of the current search).
```

I won't list the widgets, ultimately Panel can be used with any widget right?

body:
I'm not sure that having a `connectPanel` would be easier than just checking for the `items` length (or any condition that works for you).

Also I'm not sure to see an easy way to hide the fact that in order for the panel to work, you need to notify it when your condition is met.

Fine with me. We can not enforce anything of the panel stylesheet, but decline it depending on the widget. 

Also, I didn't add the Panel feature to the MultiRanges regarding the fact that the list is provided manually by the user. Do you have something in mind for this widget?

As for now, I implemented it for widgets I thought it makes sense that's why I list them here. (but we could also have written a guide). 

I don't now if allowing something like below is pertinent: 

```js
<Panel>
    <HitsPerPage items=[]/>
</Panel>
```

No but users might use it like that:

```jsx
<Panel>
  <YourCart />
</Panel>
```

```jsx
<Panel>
  <Partners>
     <UPS/>
  </Partners>
</Panel>
```

If there's no constraint on Panel usage (= can be used on any widget) then we do not need to list the widgets that have a specific behavior when used with Panel (that's a bonus, not a usage cosntraint)

Otherwise as a user you might have to parse through the whole list to know if you can use Panel (while you can definitely use it anywhere). And we will forget about maintaining the list.
